front: Le Canard enchaîné paraît tous les mercredis.
pronunciation: [luh kah-nar ahn-sheh-NAY pah-reh too lay mehr-kruh-DEE]
back: Le Canard enchaîné comes out every Wednesday.
context: A satirical weekly founded in 1915. It takes no advertising and breaks major scandals.

front: Charlie Hebdo est un journal satirique.
back: Charlie Hebdo is a satirical newspaper.
context: After the January 2015 attack, millions marched under the slogan 'Je suis Charlie'.

front: La satire est une tradition française depuis Molière et Voltaire.
pronunciation: [lah sah-TEER eh tün trah-dee-SYOHN frahn-SEZ duh-pwee moh-LYEHR ay vol-TEHR]
back: Satire has been a French tradition since Molière and Voltaire.
context: 'La satire' (mockery) ≠ 'le satyre' (a lecher, a mythical creature).

front: En France, le blasphème n'est pas un délit.
pronunciation: [ahn FRAHNS, luh blas-FEM neh pah zan day-LEE]
back: In France, blasphemy is not an offense.
context: Mocking religions is legal; inciting hatred against people is not.

front: On peut rire de tout, mais pas avec n'importe qui.
pronunciation: [ohn puh reer duh TOO, meh pah ah-vek nan-port KEE]
back: You can laugh about anything, but not with just anyone.
context: Pierre Desproges, master of dark humor.

front: Cette caricature a fait scandale.
back: This cartoon caused an outcry.
context: 'Faire scandale' = to cause a scandal.

front: Le dessin de presse résume l'actualité en une image.
pronunciation: [luh deh-san duh PRES ray-züm lak-tü-ah-lee-TAY ahn nün nee-MAHZH]
back: The press cartoon sums up the news in one image.
context: Plantu drew the front-page cartoon of Le Monde for nearly 50 years.

front: Le Gorafi publie de fausses nouvelles pour faire rire.
pronunciation: [luh goh-rah-FEE pü-blee duh fohs noo-VEL poor fehr REER]
back: Le Gorafi publishes fake news stories to make people laugh.
context: A parody of Le Figaro, the French equivalent of The Onion. Some readers take it seriously!

front: Les Guignols de l'info se moquaient des politiques avec des marionnettes.
pronunciation: [lay gee-NYOL duh lan-FOH suh moh-keh day poh-lee-TEEK ah-vek day mah-ryoh-NET]
back: Les Guignols de l'info mocked politicians with puppets.
context: A cult satirical TV show on Canal+ (1988–2018).

front: C'est du second degré.
back: It's meant ironically.
context: 'Le second degré' = irony, not meant literally. 'Au premier degré' = literally.

front: Il n'a pas compris l'humour au second degré.
pronunciation: [eel nah pah kohm-pree lü-moor oh suh-gohn duh-GRAY]
back: He didn't get the irony.
context: Missing 'le second degré' is a classic cultural misunderstanding.

front: Elle pratique l'autodérision avec talent.
back: She's very good at laughing at herself.
context: 'L'autodérision' = self-mockery, much appreciated in France.

front: Bravo, quel génie !
back: Well done, genius!
context: Said ironically after someone makes an obvious mistake.

front: Il pleut le jour de notre pique-nique, comme par hasard.
pronunciation: [eel pluh luh zhoor duh noh-truh peek-NEEK, kum par ah-ZAR]
back: It's raining on the day of our picnic, what a surprise.
context: 'Comme par hasard' (as if by chance) is ironic, or suggests a suspicious coincidence.

front: Il dit qu'il a tout fait tout seul ? Ben voyons !
pronunciation: [eel dee keel ah too feh too SUL ? ban vwah-YOHN]
back: He says he did it all by himself? Yeah, right!
context: 'Ben voyons !' = sarcastic disbelief.

front: Sans blague ? Je n'aurais jamais deviné.
back: No kidding? I'd never have guessed.
context: 'Sans blague' = no kidding (ironic or surprised).

front: Il est en retard ? Tu m'étonnes !
back: He's late? What a surprise!
context: 'Tu m'étonnes' = ironic: of course, unsurprisingly.

front: Je dis ça, je dis rien.
back: Just saying.
context: Making a pointed remark while pretending not to.

front: Ah, la belle affaire !
back: So what? Big deal!
context: Ironic: dismisses something as unimportant.

front: Il ne manquait plus que ça !
back: That's all we needed!
context: Ironic exasperation when things go from bad to worse.

front: Et le pompon, c'est qu'il a oublié les billets.
pronunciation: [ay luh pohm-POHN, seh keel ah oo-blee-ay lay bee-YEH]
back: And to top it all, he forgot the tickets.
context: 'C'est le pompon !' = that takes the cake.

front: Le ridicule ne tue pas.
back: Nobody ever died of embarrassment.
context: Often said ironically about someone who should be embarrassed.

front: Le journal a sorti un scoop.
back: The newspaper broke a scoop.
context: Also 'une exclusivité'.

front: Mediapart a révélé l'affaire Cahuzac en 2012.
pronunciation: [may-dyah-PAR ah ray-vay-lay lah-fehr kah-ü-ZAK ahn duh-meel-DOOZ]
back: Mediapart broke the Cahuzac affair in 2012.
context: The budget minister had a secret Swiss account. A landmark of investigative journalism.

front: Cette enquête a duré deux ans.
back: This investigation took two years.
context: 'Le journalisme d'investigation' = investigative journalism.

front: Plusieurs journaux ont collaboré aux Panama Papers.
pronunciation: [plü-zyuhr zhoor-NOH ohn koh-lah-boh-RAY oh pah-nah-mah pay-PUHR]
back: Several newspapers worked together on the Panama Papers.
context: An international consortium of journalists (2016).

front: Il m'a dit ça en off.
back: He told me that off the record.
context: 'En off' = off the record.

front: Le journal a dû publier un droit de réponse.
pronunciation: [luh zhoor-NAL ah dü pü-blee-ay an drwah duh ray-POHNS]
back: The paper had to publish a right of reply.
context: A legal right for anyone named in an article since 1881.

front: Il a porté plainte pour diffamation.
back: He sued for defamation.
context: 'Porter plainte' = to file a complaint.

front: La loi de 1881 garantit la liberté de la presse.
pronunciation: [lah lwah duh meel wee-sahn kah-truh-van-ON gah-rahn-TEE lah lee-behr-tay duh lah PRES]
back: The 1881 law guarantees press freedom.
context: Still the foundation of French media law.

front: L'affaire fait la une de tous les journaux.
pronunciation: [lah-FEHR feh lah ÜN duh too lay zhoor-NOH]
back: The affair is on the front page of every paper.
context: 'La une' = the front page.

front: Elle est pigiste pour plusieurs magazines.
back: She's a freelance journalist for several magazines.
context: 'Un(e) pigiste' is paid 'à la pige' (per piece).

front: Son billet d'humeur est très attendu chaque matin.
pronunciation: [sohn bee-yeh dü-MUHR eh treh zah-tahn-DÜ shak mah-TAN]
back: His opinion column is eagerly awaited every morning.
context: 'Un billet d'humeur' = a short, opinionated column, often on radio.

front: La presse people traque les célébrités.
back: The celebrity press hounds stars.
context: 'People' is pronounced 'pee-pol' in French.

front: Les paparazzis l'attendaient devant l'hôtel.
back: The paparazzi were waiting for him outside the hotel.
context: French often adds an s to the Italian plural.

front: Ce journaliste est connu pour son ton mordant.
pronunciation: [suh zhoor-nah-leest eh koh-nü poor sohn tohn mor-DAHN]
back: This journalist is known for his biting tone.
context: 'Mordant' = biting, scathing.

front: Il manie l'ironie avec finesse.
back: He handles irony with subtlety.
context: 'Manier' = to handle, wield.

front: Son humour pince-sans-rire déroute les étrangers.
back: His deadpan humor baffles foreigners.
context: 'Pince-sans-rire' = deadpan.

front: C'est l'arroseur arrosé.
back: He's been hoist with his own petard.
context: From the Lumière brothers' 1895 comic film: the waterer gets watered.

front: La satire vise les puissants, pas les faibles.
pronunciation: [lah sah-TEER veez lay pwee-SAHN, pah lay FEH-bluh]
back: Satire targets the powerful, not the weak.
context: A common defense of satirical humor.

front: Cet humoriste est passé maître dans l'art de la parodie.
pronunciation: [seh tü-moh-reest eh pah-say MEH-truh dahn lar duh lah pah-roh-DEE]
back: This comedian is a master of parody.
context: 'Passer maître dans' = to become an expert in.

front: Le président a été la cible des humoristes toute la semaine.
pronunciation: [luh pray-zee-DAHN ah ay-tay lah SEE-bluh day zü-moh-REEST toot lah suh-MEN]
back: The president was the comedians' target all week.
context: 'La cible' = target.

front: C'est un poisson d'avril !
back: It's an April Fool's joke!
context: On April 1, children stick paper fish on people's backs; the media publish hoaxes.

front: Mieux vaut en rire qu'en pleurer.
back: Better to laugh than to cry about it.
context: Humor as a way of coping.

front: Le rire corrige les mœurs.
back: Laughter corrects morals.
context: French version of the Latin motto 'castigat ridendo mores', long associated with classical comedy and Molière.
